chunks: 1668 - Fudayl ibn 'Uthman al-A'war narrated from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام that he said:

“There is no newborn except that he is born upon the fitrah. Then it is his two parents who make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله granted dhimmah and accepted jizyah from the heads of those specific people themselves on the condition that they would not make their children Jews or Christians. As for the children of the people of dhimmah today, there is no dhimmah for them.”

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: the people living under dhimmah protection
key_terms.الذِّمَّةَ: protected covenantal status granted under Islamic rule
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةَ: the poll tax accepted from non-Muslim protected subjects
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: the innate natural disposition upon which a child is born
key_terms.يُمَجِّسَانِهِ: make him Magian; cause him to adopt Magianism
key_terms.يُنَصِّرَانِهِ: make him Christian; cause him to adopt Christianity
key_terms.يُهَوِّدَانِهِ: make him Jewish; cause him to adopt Judaism

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean by every child being born upon the fitrah, and how does it relate to the children of Ahl al-Dhimmah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that every child is born upon the fitrah, while later religious affiliation is shaped by parents. It also discusses a legal condition tied to dhimmah and jizyah in relation to the religious status of children, distinguishing an earlier arrangement from the ruling concerning the children of Ahl al-Dhimmah in the present context of the narration.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1668 - Fudayl ibn Uthman al-A‘war narrated from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"Every child is born upon the natural disposition (fitrah). It is the parents who make them Jews, Christians, or Magians.
Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, granted protection (dhimmah) and accepted the payment of jizya from their adults, provided that they would not convert their children to Judaism or Christianity.
As for the children of the people of the dhimmah today, they no longer have this protected status."
